summary.text: Welson Chang, a Republican and Queens United Party small-business owner, lost the November 3, 2026 election for New York State Assembly District 24 to incumbent David Weprin.

He describes himself as a naturalized U.S. citizen who founded a manufacturing business in 2020 after a decade in nonprofit administration, and had not previously held elected office. His campaign priorities included lowering taxes, supporting small businesses and keeping Regents exam requirements.

paragraphs.text: According to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, Chang graduated from Massena Central High School and earned a B.A. in history from McGill University (2000) and an M.S. in accountancy from the University of Phoenix (2020). He describes himself as a naturalized U.S. citizen since 2008.
He says he spent a decade in nonprofit administration before entering the private sector in 2013, and founded a manufacturing business in 2020.
Chang became a county committee member in 2022, according to his survey, and says he serves on the boards of the Queens Village Republican Club and the Hollis Court at Bayside Coop.
He was not formally endorsed by the Queens County Republican Party as of April 2026, and he advanced to the general election without a primary after the June 23 Republican primary was canceled.
During the 2026 campaign he spoke at Queens Village Republican Club events in Bayside and Alley Pond Park.
He received 24.1% of the vote to David Weprin's 75.7%, according to unofficial results reported by Ballotpedia and Wikipedia.
